title: How to Prepare a Script and Brief for a Voice Over Artist
h1: How to prepare a script and brief for a voice over artist
description: Prepare a voice over script that records smoothly: word count and timing, pronunciation notes, tone references, file specs, revisions and usage rights.
intro: A voice over is only as good as the script and instructions behind it. Most retakes happen not because the voice artist made a mistake, but because the script was unclear, too long for the video, or full of names nobody explained how to say. A little preparation leads to a recording that fits your video on the first try. This article explains how to prepare the script, the brief and the technical details before you hire.

faq.q: How many words fit in a minute?
faq.a: Roughly 130 to 160 words per minute for natural narration, fewer for slow, calm reads.

faq.q: Can I change the script after recording?
faq.a: Usually that counts as a new recording or a paid revision, so finalize the script first.

faq.q: What file format should I ask for?
faq.a: WAV for editing and best quality, MP3 for quick previews, at the sample rate your editor needs.

faq.q: Do I need to explain pronunciation?
faq.a: Yes, for names, brands, acronyms and technical words. A short audio example helps most.
Permission to use the recording in specific places, such as online, broadcast or paid ads.
